output.rationale: Teach a compact membrane transport model first, then require learners to explain it, repair gaps, and reexplain before a final recognition check.

essentialIdeas: Phospholipid bilayers are selectively permeable because hydrophilic heads face water while hydrophobic tails block many polar or charged substances.
Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport uses energy to move substances against a gradient.
completionEvidence: Explain why a phospholipid bilayer is selectively permeable.
Classify a transport example as passive or active and justify it.

activities.title: Membrane structure and permeability
activities.body: Read the model and note the key relationship.

essentialIdeas: Phospholipid bilayers are selectively permeable because hydrophilic heads face water while hydrophobic tails block many polar or charged substances.

activities.label: Explain the barrier
activities.title: Why membranes block some substances
activities.body: Explain the relationship in your own words.
activities.concept: Phospholipid bilayers are selectively permeable because hydrophilic heads face water while hydrophobic tails block many
activities.correctAnswer: The phospholipid bilayer is selectively permeable because the hydrophobic tails form a barrier that blocks many polar or charged substances while the hydrophilic heads face water.
activities.feedback: A complete answer explains the water-facing heads, the nonpolar tails, and why that limits some substances from crossing.

activities.label: Fix the transport rule
activities.title: Passive versus active transport
activities.body: Fix the mistake and give a corrected rule.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Thinking active transport is just any movement across the membrane, instead of energy-requiring movement against a gradient.
activities.concept: Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport
activities.correctAnswer: Passive transport moves substances down a concentration gradient without energy, while active transport uses energy to move substances against a gradient.
activities.feedback: The correction must separate movement with the gradient from movement against it and include energy only for active transport.

activities.label: State the full model
activities.title: Explain both transport ideas
activities.body: Explain the full model again in plain language.
activities.concept: Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport
activities.correctAnswer: Passive transport moves substances down a concentration gradient without energy, while active transport uses energy to move substances against a gradient.
activities.feedback: A strong response clearly contrasts direction of movement and energy use, then connects that contrast to membrane transport.

activities.label: Classify one case
activities.title: Transport classification check
activities.body: Choose the best classification for the case.
activities.concept: Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport
choices: Neither requires movement across a membrane
activities.feedback: Active transport is the choice when energy is used to move substances against a concentration gradient.

items.essentialIdea: Phospholipid tails and heads create a membrane barrier that blocks most polar solutes.

check.title: Phospholipid barrier role
check.prompt: How does phospholipid structure make the membrane selectively permeable?
check.referenceAnswer: Hydrophilic heads face water and hydrophobic tails face inward, forming a barrier that resists most polar or charged solutes.
check.feedback: Correct: the inward-facing hydrophobic tails are the key barrier.

items.essentialIdea: Passive transport moves substances down gradients without cellular energy, while active transport uses energy against gradients.

check.title: Passive versus active movement
check.prompt: How do passive transport and active transport differ across a membrane?
check.referenceAnswer: Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without energy, while active transport uses cellular energy to move substances against a gradient.
check.feedback: Correct: the direction relative to the gradient and energy use distinguish them.

recognitionCheck.title: Identify transport type
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which statement correctly describes active transport?
choices: It moves substances down their concentration gradient without energy.
It uses cellular energy to move substances against a concentration gradient.
It occurs only through phospholipid tails.
It always moves water out of the cell.
recognitionCheck.correctAnswer: It uses cellular energy to move substances against a concentration gradient.
recognitionCheck.feedback: Correct: active transport requires energy and moves against the gradient.
